source.name: Curious claims
source.note: The claim pipeline (packages/curious-pipeline) discovers documents from GDELT news, the Library of Congress, Europeana and Gallica, splits passages into atomic claims each with a verbatim evidence quote of at most 300 characters, groups every supporting source into an independence lineage (one wire story retold twenty times is one lineage), grades each claim A to E from explicit features (a primary source, independent contemporaneous lineages, institutional quality, a quotation found in print, chronology and geography against the entities, scholarship cited; minus anonymous repetition, circular citation, a time gap, a translation, a contradiction), and a human approves it on the admin Curious claims tab. The desk draws only approved claims. The grade is a computed reading of the sources found so far: it goes on the page as the desk's grade, and the research may argue for another.

eras.name: The long nineteenth century
eras.description: 1790 to the eve of the First World War.

eras.name: Undated
eras.description: The claim names no year: the research dates it or says why it cannot be dated.

themes.name: Science and invention
themes.description: Discoveries, machines, medicine, the people who made them and the accidents along the way.

themes.name: Arts and music
themes.description: Painting, sculpture, theatre, songs, concerts and the stories around them.

themes.name: Film and television
themes.description: Films, shows, stars, box offices and audiences in unexpected places.

themes.name: Food and drink
themes.description: Dishes, ingredients, recipes, famines, feasts and the trade behind them.

themes.name: Sport and games
themes.description: Matches, records, players, rules and the games people played.

themes.name: Words and language
themes.description: Etymologies, scripts, translations, slang and misprints that stuck.

themes.name: Money and trade
themes.description: Prices, currencies, companies, bubbles and what things cost.

themes.name: War and peace
themes.description: Battles, truces, spies, deserters and the odd detail the record kept.

themes.name: Law and crime
themes.description: Trials, laws, heists, punishments and the rules people broke.

themes.name: Cities and buildings
themes.description: Streets, bridges, towers, plans that failed and buildings that moved.

themes.name: Nature and animals
themes.description: Weather, creatures, plants, disasters and the animals in human stories.

themes.name: Travel and transport
themes.description: Ships, trains, balloons, roads, journeys and the first and last of each.

A.label: Direct primary evidence plus independent corroboration
A.rule: The page may state it as fact, with the primary source linked.

B.label: Strong contemporaneous evidence or multiple independent reputable sources
B.rule: The page may state it as fact, naming the sources.

C.label: Plausible and well-sourced secondary account; primary evidence not located
C.rule: The page says who reports it and that no primary record was found.

D.label: Repeated anecdote whose evidentiary chain traces to an unsourced account
D.rule: The page may only say that it is widely repeated and by whom, never that it happened, until the research finds better.

E.label: Contradicted, impossible, circular or unsupported
E.rule: The page states the contradiction or the gap; the claim itself is not asserted.

lenses.name: Trace the lineage
lenses.description: Follow the story back: who told it first, who copied whom, where the wording changed, and what the earliest source actually says. The page is the family tree of a claim.

lenses.name: Core vs embellishment
lenses.description: Split the claim into the part the record supports and the part that grew on it: two claims, two grades, side by side, and how the second attached itself to the first.

lenses.name: The number behind it
lenses.description: Take the figure in the claim (the admissions, the years, the tonnes) back to its source, test it against other counts, and show what it would mean if true.

lenses.name: Where it happened
lenses.description: Put the claim on the map: the place as the sources name it and as it is now, what else was there at the time, and whether the geography makes the story possible.

lenses.name: Then and now
lenses.description: The claim's world against today's: what the thing cost, counted or weighed then and now, and what changed in between.

lenses.name: Who says so
lenses.description: The sources as characters: the archive, the memoirist, the wire reporter, the blogger. What each could know, what each wanted, and where they disagree.

lenses.name: Explain like I'm 5
lenses.description: The claim told to a five-year-old as a short picture story: one everyday stand-in, what really happened as far as anyone knows, and where the picture stops being true.
